title: Vocabulary Guessing from Text and Identifying Paragraph Main Ideas
summary: A vocabulary exercise where students guess the meaning of bold words from an earlier reading, then a guided lesson on finding the main idea of a paragraph with sample answer analysis showing why incorrect choices don't match.

title: Finding Main Ideas in Multiple Paragraphs and Rewriting Sentences with Should
summary: Students read four paragraphs of a text and choose the correct main idea for each, then rewrite sentences using should or shouldn't based on given situations.

title: Study Tip on Skimming and Scanning with Comprehension Exercises
summary: A study tip explaining skimming and scanning techniques, followed by a scanning multiple-choice activity about a robbery story and detailed reading questions about what happened.

title: Formal and Informal Word Pairs with Have, Get and Make Grammar Practice
summary: An exercise matching formal words with less formal alternatives from an email, plus grammar rules and practice for using have/get plus object plus past participle and make plus object plus infinitive.

title: Reading a Home Safety Brochure with Comprehension and Vocabulary Tasks
summary: Questions about a home safety brochure covering theft prevention, a vocabulary matching exercise, and an analysis of persuasive writing techniques such as questions, exclamations, and strong adjectives.

title: Identifying Strong Adverbs and Writing Reasons for Home Safety Practices
summary: Continues analysing persuasive techniques with strong adverbs and examples, then asks students to evaluate home safety tips and justify why each practice is advisable or unwise.

title: Listening Task on a Driving Lesson and Preparing a Road Safety Leaflet
summary: A listening activity where students order photos mentioned in a driving lesson dialogue, then identify problems in cartoon images, and plan a road safety leaflet listing do's and don'ts with supporting reasons.

title: Writing and Revising an Essay on the Importance of Road Safety
summary: Students write a 100–120 word essay on road safety using two given paragraph headings for organization, then revise for clarity, proofread for errors, and exchange work with a partner for feedback.
